description: Long-running daemon. Every 600s, queries WriteService /query for up to 50 mcp_discovery_candidates rows where (promoted IS NOT TRUE) AND discovered_in_directory='mcp_registry'. For each candidate, GET candidate_url (e.g. https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/servers/<reverse-dns>) with timeout=15 and User-Agent 'zo-sentinel/1.0 (mcp-trust-intelligence)'. Parse the response JSON: extract server.name, server.description, server.version; extract _meta.{namespace}/official.{status, publishedAt, isLatest}; iterate packages[] which contains entries like {registryType, identifier, version, transport}. For each package, mint server_id = first 16 hex chars of MD5(registryType + '|' + identifier) lower-cased; build mcp_server_registry row {server_id, name=identifier, registry_source=registryType ('npm'|'github'|'pypi'|'oci'|other), url=derived (npm -> https://www.npmjs.com/package/{identifier}; github -> https://github.com/{identifier}; pypi -> https://pypi.org/project/{identifier}/), description (truncated to 1000), trust_score=0.0, verdict='unknown', verdict_reasoning='', confidence=0.0, last_assessed=NULL, first_seen=NOW(), last_seen=NOW(), last_scanned=NULL, scan_count=0, risk_tier='unassessed', metadata=JSON of {version, status, publishedAt, isLatest, mcp_registry_name, transport}}. POST to /write table='mcp_server_registry' with wait=True; on success POST to /execute UPDATE mcp_discovery_candidates SET promoted=TRUE, reviewed_at=NOW() WHERE id=<candidate_id>. Per-candidate exception isolation so one bad row doesn't wedge the batch. Heartbeat thread every 30s. Single-instance lockfile at /home/workspace/logs/candidate_promoter_daemon.lock with PID. NEVER imports duckdb or sqlite3. requests timeout=15 on the registry fetch, timeout=10 on /write and /execute. Inter-fetch sleep 0.25s. Logging: only FileHandler (no StreamHandler -- nohup pipes stdout to same file and StreamHandler would double every line). Logs structured INFO line per cycle: 'cycle done: candidates_seen=N promoted=M errors=K skipped=S'.
